terms.gloss: later than expected or than one said
terms.grammar: comparative adverb of tardē, with quam
evidence: Plin. Ep. 10.17A.2: aliquantō tardius quam spērāveram

phrases.english: Hurry up! We’ll be late to Grandma’s.

phrases.latin: māne venī potius; nam cūr tē quīnta morētur? ut jantēs, sērō, Caeciliāne, venīs
phrases.english: come in the morning instead; why should the fifth hour keep you? For breakfast, Caecilianus, you’re late

phrases.latin: Tardius veniam quam dīxī; nē mē exspectāverīs.
phrases.english: I’ll be later than I said; don’t wait for me.

phrases.latin: tē Rōmā … putārī profectum esse tardius quam dīxerās
phrases.english: that you are thought to have left Rome later than you had said

sources: Lewis & Short: serus · Lewis & Short: tardus
